name: Huang Zhenda

appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014); Hurun China (2008-2023); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Huang Zhenda chairs Guangdong Lian Tai Group, which is active in construction, toll road operation, property development and sewage treatment.
Huang was a construction worker before he founded Shantou Dahao Municipal Engineering Corp. in 1984, the predecessor to Guangdong Lian Tai Group.
Huang has donated more than $140 million to philanthropic causes over the years.

name: Oleg Boyko
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Oleg Boyko's private equity firm Finstar Financial currently manages and consults portfolio companies operating in 30+ countries.
After Russia invaded Ukraine, his mother who held all of his shares in fintech 4Finance gave 9.9% each to Ukrainian relatives and a nonprofit in Switzerland.
She sold the rest of the family's 4Finance stake to four new, non-Russian minority shareholders.
Boyko opened Moscow's first stores with credit card readers in the 1990s.
In 2002 Boyko invested in a Moscow chain of gambling venues and founded Ritzio Entertainment Group, which invested in casinos and gambling.
When gambling was banned, Boyko sold his Russian gambling assets and moved into gambling in the European Union.
forbes_facts: Boyko, who was injured in an accident in 1996 and often appears in a scooter-style wheelchair, is the main private sponsor of Russian Paralympics team.
He invests in movie-making. His projects include Roberto Rodriguez's Sin City II and Scarlett Johansson's Summer Crossing.

name: Jeffrey Lorberbaum
sec_insider_companies: MOHAWK INDUSTRIES INC (MHK) - CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Jeffrey Lorberbaum built Georgia-based Mohawk Industries into the largest flooring company in the world; he owns a nearly 15% stake.
His father Alan founded Aladdin Mills in 1957 as a maker of bathmats. Lorberbaum joined the company in 1976 and later became CEO.
In 1994, the family sold Aladdin to Mohawk Industries. Lorberbaum took charge of Mohawk in 2001 and expanded into hard-surface flooring.
The publicly traded flooring company is now in more than 170 countries and has completed 54 acquisitions since it went public in 1992.
forbes_facts: In 2022, Lorberbaum was given the honorary title of knight commander of the Order of the Crown by Her Royal Highness Princess Astrid of Belgium.
Lorberbaum is in the World Floor Covering Association's Hall of Fame.

name: Thomas Crowley Jr
forbes_bio: Thomas B. Crowley Jr. is the chairman and majority owner of Jacksonville, Florida-based shipping company Crowley Maritime.
He and his immediate family own some 80% of the $3.5 billion (revenue) company.
Crowley is the third generation to run the family firm, which his grandfather founded in 1892.
Crowley took over the company at the age of 27, when his dad died in 1994.
He has grown Crowley Maritime's fleet to 125 shipping vessels as of July 2025.

name: Wu Cheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026); Hurun China U40 (2022)
forbes_bio: Wu Cheng is chairman of Guocheng Mining, a Beijing-based miner of metals.
His Guocheng Co, a holding company, has interests in chemical, logistics and hotels.
Guocheng employs a staff of 7,000 and has operations across China, including Beijing, Inner Mongolia, Sichuan and Tibet, among others.

name: Sylvia Wedemeyer
forbes_bio: Sylvia Wedemeyer is a shareholder of Cordes & Graefe, the parent company of the GC Group, a wholesaler that covers a wide range of products for plumbing and HVAC systems.
Founded in 1921 as a pipe and tube trading company, Cordes & Graefe formed the GC Group in 1975 through a series of acquisitions.
Today the company is one of the largest wholesalers in the industry with $17 billion in sales (2023).
The company is 100% owned by the Hollweg family. Sylvia Wedemeyer is the daughter of longtime company leader Uwe Hollweg who died in December 2024.

name: Lu Hongyan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2023); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Lu Hongyan chairs Shanghai-listed online games company G-bits Network Technology.
Its business benefited during the pandemic, when quarantined Chinese people turned to online gaming for fun.
Lu worked for telecom firms ZTE and Salira Optical Network Systems as a software engineer before he founded G-bits in 2004.
